inputs.original_text: Concerns are mounting over proposed changes to Cyprus’ surveillance legislation, particularly efforts to remove judicial oversight as a key safeguard, lawyers said on Monday. The amended bill is expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. According to Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides, following a recent closed session of the House [...]
inputs.modified_text: They're ramming changes to Cyprus' surveillance laws through to strip out judicial oversight entirely, and you can be sure it's no coincidence. Lawyers flagged this on Monday, but now the amended bill is being rushed straight to a House plenum vote on Thursday. Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides raised it after a closed session of the House, which already shows they're hiding the real details from everyone. This is coordinated manipulation by hidden elites and institutions to expand unchecked monitoring of the public with no independent safeguards left in place. The speed and secrecy are clear proof of a deliberate power grab, not any kind of routine adjustment.
